product.askAnAdminOfThis: Ask an admin of this Identity for access.
product.youSignInToYour: You sign in to your applications with this account. Keep a second factor here: an authenticator app or a passkey.
product.addASecondFactorTo: Add a second factor to continue
product.theApplicationYouAreSigning: The application you are signing in to accepts only a passkey. Add one below, or sign out and sign in again with yours, then continue.
product.theApplicationYouAreSigning2: The application you are signing in to asks for one. Add an authenticator app or a passkey below, then continue.

samlDetails.inIamIdentityCenterOpen: In IAM Identity Center, open Settings, Identity source, and change it to an external identity provider. Upload Identity's metadata, downloaded from the address above; AWS shows its ACS URL and issuer, which you entered here. Name people in AWS by their email.
samlDetails.giveTheApplicationIdentityS: Give the application Identity's metadata address, or the entity ID, sign-in URL and certificate. Identity signs the response and the assertion with RSA-SHA256, and sends the attributes email, name and groups.

created.identityKeepsItEncryptedAnd: Identity keeps it encrypted and does not show it again; a new one can be made later.
created.inOpenSettingsSignIn: In {{product}}, open Settings, Sign-in, add a provider and choose OpenAsy Identity, then enter these. Or set them in its environment and restart it:
created.setTheApplicationUpWith: Set the application up with them; it must send PKCE (S256), and asks for the scopes openid, email, profile and groups.
created.closingThisDialogHidesThe: Closing this dialog hides the secret

addApplication.peopleSignInToIt: People sign in to it with Identity. Choose who may.
addApplication.name: Name
addApplication.whoTheApplicationIsThe: Who the application is: the audience of Identity's answers.
addApplication.whereItReceivesAnswersIdentity: Where it receives answers. Identity answers only here.
addApplication.aStableIdThatNever: A stable id that never changes
addApplication.itsCallbackAddressesAreFilled: Its callback addresses are filled in.
addApplication.httpsOrHttpOnLocalhost: https, or http on localhost; several separated by spaces.
addApplication.noGroupsYetAddOne: No groups yet: add one under Groups, or let everyone in.

applicationsPage.makeANewSecretFor: Make a new secret for {{name}}? The old one stops working at once.
applicationsPage.removeNobodyCanSignIn: Remove {{name}}? Nobody can sign in to it with Identity any more.
applicationsPage.applicationsSignPeopleInWith: Applications sign people in with OpenID Connect at the issuer {{issuer}}.
applicationsPage.applicationsSignPeopleInWith2: Applications sign people in with OpenID Connect.

addDirectory.useAReadOnlyService: Use a read-only service account. Filters left empty use the ones shown.
addDirectory.shownToPeopleAsWhere: Shown to people as where their password is kept.
addDirectory.groupsThatMatchFollowThe: Groups that match follow the directory, with their members.

directoriesPage.removeItsPeopleAreTurned: Remove {{name}}? Its {{people}} people are turned off: their password was its.
directoriesPage.identityReadsPeopleAndGroups: Identity reads people and groups from Active Directory or LDAP on a schedule. Its people sign in with the password it keeps, checked there; people who leave or are disabled there are turned off here. People who manage Identity are never changed by it.

members.theyCanSignInTo: They can sign in to the applications this group may use, and the group goes to those applications in the groups claim.

groupsPage.removeItsMembersLoseThe: Remove {{name}}? Its members lose the applications only it gave them.
groupsPage.groupsDecideWhoMaySign: Groups decide who may sign in to which application, and applications receive them to give people roles. Where a second factor is required, members sign in to applications with an authenticator app, a passkey or an identity provider.
groupsPage.thenChooseItsMembersAnd: Then choose its members, and which applications it may sign in to.
groupsPage.name: Name
groupsPage.optionalProviderIdGroupThere: Optional: <provider id>:<group there>. Members then follow that group at each sign-in.

overviewPage.singleSignOnForOpenasy: Single sign-on for OpenAsy products and any other application, with MFA and passkeys.
overviewPage.addAnApplicationChooseThe: Add an application, choose the groups that may use it, and people sign in to it with Identity.
overviewPage.nobodySignedInToAn: Nobody signed in to an application yet
overviewPage.signInWithAPassword: Sign in with a password alone
overviewPage.noAuthenticatorAppNoPasskey: No authenticator app, no passkey and no identity provider. Groups that require a second factor send them to add one.

auditPage.signInsAndChangesNewest: Sign-ins and changes, newest first, kept 400 days. Each is also written to the log as JSON, for your SIEM.

peoplePage.name: Name
peoplePage.everyoneWhoSignsInTo: Everyone who signs in to applications with Identity. People from an identity provider appear after their first sign-in; disable or remove someone under Members.
peoplePage.sendThisLinkToThem: Send this link to them yourself; it works once, until {{value}}.
peoplePage.closingThisDialogHidesThe: Closing this dialog hides the link
peoplePage.theyGetALinkTo: They get a link to choose a password. They can sign in to the applications their groups allow, not manage Identity.

provisioningPage.oktaMicrosoftEntraIdAnd: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID and other identity providers create, change and remove people and groups here with SCIM 2.0. When someone leaves, the provider turns them off and they lose every application at once. It never changes the people who manage Identity.
provisioningPage.offMakeATokenTo: Off: make a token to turn it on.
provisioningPage.makeANewTokenThe: Make a new token? The provider's current one stops working at once.
provisioningPage.turnScimOffTheProvider: Turn SCIM off? The provider can no longer change anyone here.
provisioningPage.identityKeepsOnlyItsHash: Identity keeps only its hash. Enter it in the provider as the bearer token, or secret token, with the base URL above.
provisioningPage.oktaInTheAppProvisioning: Okta: in the app, Provisioning, choose SCIM 2.0 with HTTP header authentication, enter the base URL and the token, and turn on creating, updating and deactivating users and pushing groups.
provisioningPage.microsoftEntraIdInThe: Microsoft Entra ID: in the enterprise application, Provisioning, choose Automatic, enter the base URL as the tenant URL and the token as the secret token, and test the connection.
provisioningPage.peopleProvisionedThisWaySign: People provisioned this way sign in through that provider: add it under Sign-in, and they are matched by their verified email.

settings.accountText: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.
settings.membersText: Who can manage this Identity, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also change groups; admins also manage applications, providers, members and tokens. People with the User role only sign in to applications.
settings.signinText: Identity providers people can sign in to Identity with, such as Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.
settings.tokensText: For scripts. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
